newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour eyes reform of competition law.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour eyes reform of competition law.

text.p: Britain's Labour Party will introduce a bill to overhaul Britain's competition law and institutions if it wins the coming election, its leader Tony Blair said on Tuesday.
He told a business conference the case for reform was strong. He said a new law, which Labour would seek to introduce soon after taking office would seek to:
-- prevent and remedy anti-competitive behaviour more effectively
-- reduce the administrative burden for business
-- review the extent of ministerial involvement in decision making

Labour has until now favoured merging the Office of Fair Trading and the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. It has also been keen on introducing a requirement that mergers should be demonstrably in the public interest.
On Tuesday, however, Blair backed away from these commitments and said he would ask a panel of three "wise men" to examine the issues further and make recommendations to the Labour leadership.
The move follows objections to Labour's ideas by a prestigious Business Commission set up by the left-leaning Institute for Public Policy Research think-tank.

Blair said, however, that Labour and the Commission, whose members include a number of prominent businessmen, agreed on the most important issues -- the need to adopt a prohibitive approach to provide strong deterrence to restrictive agreements and abuses of market power; and more effective penalties against proven anti-competitive behaviour. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
